headword: {一長一短|いっちょういったん}

definitions.gloss: pros and cons, merits and demerits
definitions.explanation: Having both good and bad points. Literally: one long, one short.

examples.japanese: どちらにも{一長一短|いっちょういったん}がある。
examples.english: Both have their pros and cons.

examples.japanese: {一長一短|いっちょういったん}を{比|くら}べて{決|き}めた。
examples.english: I compared the pros and cons and decided.

examples.japanese: {都会|とかい}{暮|く}らしには{一長一短|いっちょういったん}がある。
examples.english: Living in the city has its advantages and disadvantages.

examples.japanese: どの{方法|ほうほう}にも{一長一短|いっちょういったん}があるので、よく{考|かんが}えてから{選|えら}んだほうがいい。
examples.english: Every method has its pros and cons, so you should think carefully before choosing.

examples.japanese: {電車|でんしゃ}も{車|くるま}も{一長一短|いっちょういったん}だが、{時間|じかん}が{読|よ}めるという{点|てん}では{電車|でんしゃ}のほうがいい。
examples.english: Both trains and cars have pros and cons, but trains are better in that the travel time is predictable.

notes:
{一長一短|いっちょういったん} is a {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} meaning "pros and cons" or "merits and demerits."

LITERAL MEANING:
{一|いち} (one) + {長|ちょう} (strong point) + {一|いち} (one) + {短|たん} (weak point) - "one strength, one weakness."

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {一長一短|いっちょういったん}がある: has pros and cons
- {一長一短|いっちょういったん}を{比|くら}べる: compare the pros and cons
- どちらにも{一長一短|いっちょういったん}がある: both have their merits and demerits

USAGE:
Used when evaluating options where nothing is perfect. Conveys that each choice has both advantages and disadvantages.

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- メリット・デメリット: merits and demerits (loanword)
- {長所|ちょうしょ}と{短所|たんしょ}: strengths and weaknesses
